Greg Lopez

Unaffiliated candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Colorado · Open seat

Former U.S. Representative and former Mayor of Parker

Greg Lopez is a former Republican who represented Colorado's 4th Congressional District for about six months in 2024, after winning a special election to fill the seat Ken Buck left. He had sought the Republican nomination for governor in 2018 and 2022. He left the GOP in January 2026 and got on the November ballot as an unaffiliated candidate by petition, which the Secretary of State's office confirmed on July 28, 2026.

Where Lopez stands

Housing and cost of living
Proposes building 25,000 starter homes in his first four years, focused on modest two-bedroom units that could cost as little as $235,000.
Housing and cost of living
Says he would cut regulations, fees and permitting delays that he says raise housing, energy, insurance, transportation and grocery costs.
Size of government
Says his top priority would be a Colorado 'Department of Government Efficiency' that reviews every agency and program to cut waste, duplication, unnecessary regulation and inefficient spending.
TABOR and state budget
Says he wants to reform TABOR through a grassroots, bottom-up effort that would include changes to the state tax system and to constitutional spending limits.
State budget / structural deficit
Says the structural deficit cannot be solved with temporary fixes, accounting maneuvers or across-the-board cuts to essential services, and that the structure of spending itself must change.
Technology regulation
Said in an August 2026 debate that the jury is still out on data centers, and that he is worried about their water use.
Medicaid
Proposes help for rural hospitals.

Background

  • Mayor of Parker, Colorado (former)
  • U.S. Representative, Colorado's 4th Congressional District (2024; won a special election to finish Ken Buck's term)
  • Ran for the Republican nomination for governor (2018, 2022; lost both primaries)
  • Left the Republican Party and announced an unaffiliated run for governor (January 2026)
  • Qualified for the 2026 general-election ballot by petition (verified July 28, 2026)
